On August 1, the Kazakh Energy Ministry reported that the CPC was receiving 100,000 metric tons of crude per day, however, while the pipeline can continue transporting crude from Kazakhstan to storage facilities while awaiting maritime export, if storage tanks fill, the CPC may have to restrict intake, forcing Kazakh producers to restrict output.

incidents.title: Central Asia Aligns With China on AI
incidents.description: Representatives from Central Asian states attended a Beijing conference on AI. At this meeting, they signed an agreement to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO) and multiple agreements to enhance cooperation on AI, digital infrastructure, and other tech sectors, totalling tens of billions USD.

incidents.title: Tajikistan Triples Central Asian Fuel Imports
incidents.description: As Russian fuel deliveries continue to decline, Tajikistan has increased fuel imports from its Central Asian neighbors. Dushanbe imported approximately 34,000 tons of fuel from Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and Kazakhstan in July, which is almost triple the recorded import volume in June.

incidents.title: Putative Azerbaijan-Turkmenistan Business Council Discusses New Trade Avenues
incidents.description: Azerbaijan Minister of Economy Mikayil Jabbarov spoke with Turkmenistan's Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Nokerguly Atahulyev, about establishing a Turkmen-Azerbaijani Business Council that would expand trade in energy, agriculture, and other goods. No agreements were reached at this meeting.

incidents.title: China, Kazakhstan Commence Joint Earthquake Research in Almaty
incidents.description: China and Kazakhstan have begun joint earthquake research in Almaty, Kazakhstan, following the opening of the future Kazakhstan-China Joint Earthquake Research Centre building. The centre for this research has already been established within Kazakhstan's National Scientific Centre for Seismology, but is pending the official signing of an intergovernmental agreement.

incidents.title: President Trump Discusses US-Uzbek Relationship with Counterpart
incidents.description: President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a telephone conversation with President Trump, who stated that Uzbek-American relations had reached an “unprecedented level” over the past year. The Presidents expressed a joint belief that the introduction of a visa-free regime for U.S. citizens is helping to increase business integration between the countries. Joint projects are ongoing between Uzbekistan and the United States in the areas of aviation, mining, energy, metallurgy, and artificial intelligence. At the end of the call, President Mirziyoyev invited President Trump to officially visit Uzbekistan during his term.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Signs Agreement with US Company on Industrial Water Treatment
incidents.description: Following a meeting in Astana, a memorandum of cooperation was signed by the National Hydrological-Geological Service Kazhydrogeology, US-based IBL Elements, and representatives of Kazakhstan’s oil and gas companies, according to Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation. The meeting was focused on the implementation of technologies for studying, treating, and using water produced during oil and gas operations. The agreement provides a framework for the introduction of new technological solutions in industrial water operations.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Environmental Researchers Propose Chinese Technology Tests
incidents.description: Kazakhstan's environmental association proposed trials of Chinese technology, studied by Kazakhstani researchers in Hunan province, to address Kazakhstan's degraded pastureland and erosion issues. Researchers were interested in using targeted spraying, biological fertilizers, and specialized seed treatment to reduce chemical pesticide usage.

incidents.title: Automated Water Monitoring Coming to Syr Darya River
incidents.description: Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and Kazakhstan agreed to automate monitoring of water levels and flows on the Syr Darya river. If successful, this will help manage the resource and prevent $4.5 billion in economic losses annually.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan launches Seasonal Work Program in Partnership with US Company
incidents.description: Uzbekistan’s Migration Agency announced that it has partnered with an undisclosed US recruitment company to send citizens to the United States for seasonal agricultural work under the H-2A visa program. Select Uzbek citizens will be provided with temporary non-immigrant visas and will work on US farms harvesting and assisting with other farm work. Workers will not be permitted to independently seek other employment or change employers under the H-2A visa.

incidents.title: Uzbek and Chinese Metallurgical Companies Sign Cooperation Memorandum
incidents.description: Uzbek company Uzmekombinat JSC and Chinese company Metallurgical Corporation of China CERI signed a strategic cooperation memorandum to advance metallurgical projects in Uzbekistan. The memorandum serves as a foundation for executing projects that aim to expand Uzmekombinat's production, increase its access to raw materials, and apply new engineering solutions.

incidents.title: Eight Uzbeks Killed in Ukrainian Drone Attack
incidents.description: Uzbekistan has sent a special task force to Russia to retrieve the bodies of eight of its citizens who died in a Ukrainian drone attack on industrial facilities in Russia's Tatarstan region. The drone attack reportedly killed 13 people, including one child, and left over 70 seeking medical assistance. Citizens of Uzbekistan and Tajikistan were among the victims.

incidents.title: Kazakhstani President to Attend G20 Meeting as Guest of Trump
incidents.description: Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on August 12th that President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev will attend the G20 Summit on December 14th at President Donald Trump’s golf resort in Florida. Kazakhstan is not a member of the G20, but will attend as a guest of the US. Ties between Kazakhstan and the US have deepened in recent years. One of Washington’s G20 goals is critical mineral extraction, and Kazakhstan is the world’s largest uranium producer. Tokayev also had his country join Trump’s Board of Peace in early 2026.

incidents.title: Threat of US Sanctions on Russia Leads to Preemptive Compliance Measures in Kazakhstan
incidents.description: Recent developments indicate that the new US approach towards Russia may have a major impact on Kazakhstan. Legislation that would dramatically expand President Trump’s authority to impose secondary sanctions against countries and companies helping Russia evade sanctions has overwhelmingly passed the Senate, and as a result Kazakh banks are already tightening compliance to minimize sanction impact. Energy exports are also a vulnerability, but Kazakh diplomats successfully convinced the US in early August to pressure Ukraine into refraining from strikes against Russian infrastructure that exports Kazakh oil.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan Establish Joint Commission to Manage Water
incidents.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan established a Joint Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan Commission to manage shared water resources. This follows Kazakhstan's surge in water diplomacy, including its establishment of the Water Diplomacy Department in its Water Resources Ministry.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Continues Operative Role in Europe-China Trade Relations
incidents.description: Kazakhstan has been developing internal and external terminal networks on China's Yellow Sea coast and on the Black Sea. This gives Kazakhstan an operative role in trade that goes between Europe and China.

incidents.title: Blackout Hits Four Central Asian Countries
incidents.description: The energy ministries of Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan all reported power outages on Friday, August 14. These nations rely on an interconnected power grid constructed during the Soviet era. According to Kyrgyz authorities, the outage was triggered by a short-term shutdown of two generators at the Toktogul Hydroelectric Power Station, which altered regional power flows and triggered automated emergency systems. The incident underscores growing strain on Central Asia’s shared grid as electricity demand rises faster than governments can upgrade transmission and storage capacity.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Expand Agricultural Trade
incidents.description: According to the Russian Ministry of Agriculture, bilateral agricultural trade between Russia and Kyrgyzstan increased by 25% in 2025. Russia supplies sunflower oil, confectionery products, sugar, poultry, and non-alcoholic beverages to Kyrgyzstan, whereas Kyrgyzstan supplies fruit, berries, and other agricultural products to Russia.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan Discuss Transport Issues
incidents.description: Representatives of Uzbekistan's transportation sector met with Turkmenistan's government to discuss issues related to cross-border transportation. Major points of discussion were expanding cross border rail transportation, expanding Caspian Sea maritime infrastructure, and restoring civilian air transportation between Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan, China Meet to Discuss Long-Term Fuel Cooperation
incidents.description: The Uzbek state-owned company Uzbekneftegaz met with a Chinese delegation to discuss expanding fuel cooperation and investment. One key discussion during the meeting focused on the possibility of China implementing long-term imports of Jet A-1 fuel, which would diversify Uzbekistan's aviation fuel supplies.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Deepens Higher Ed Cooperation with Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan
incidents.description: Uzbekistan signed two memorandums of understanding with Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan aimed at increasing higher education exchanges. Central to these MOUs is the "Study in Uzbekistan" initiative aimed at increasing Azerbaijani and Central Asian student participation in Uzbekistan's universities.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Conduct Joint Military Exercises
incidents.description: Russian and Kyrgyz forces conducted joint military training exercises at Kyrgyzstan’s Edelweiss training ground. The exercises involved 500 servicemen from both countries along with up to 100 pieces of weapons and military equipment.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan-China Investment Forum Yields $10 Billion Worth of Potential Joint Projects
incidents.description: At the Chinese International Investment Forum hosted in Uzbekistan, Chinese investment companies were presented with over 95 potential projects valued at $10 billion in total by Uzbek government agencies. After the forum, investors and Uzbek representatives signed preliminary agreements on 63 projects, valued at over $6.25 billion.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Tightens Counterterrorism Security in Caspian Sea
incidents.description: Amendments submitted to Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Energy aim to tighten counterterrorism protections at Kazakh oil and gas facilities in the Caspian Sea. Under these proposed regulations, companies conducting subsoil operations in Kazakhstan’s Caspian territory must provide a site near production facilities for the Kazakh maritime counterterrorism operational headquarters. Operating companies will also be required to cover all deployment and expenses for the unit.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan, China Discuss Fuel Cooperation Amidst Unreliable Russian Exports
incidents.description: During a meeting with China Petroleum and Chemical Corporation (Sinopec), Kyrgyzstan's deputy chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Erlist Akunbekov, expressed interest in increasing petroleum imports from China. While Kyrgyzstan currently obtains over 90 percent of its petroleum imports from Russia, the reliability of Russian fuel imports has declined due to Ukrainian drone strikes on oil refineries and increasing export restrictions.

incidents.title: Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan Establish Electronic Exchange for Transport
incidents.description: Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan have established digital database that allows customs authorities to receive advance warning about vehicles before they arrive at the border, allowing them to prepare for immediate inspection of goods upon arrival. This reduces paperwork and reduces bottlenecks at border crossings.

incidents.title: Azerbaijan's Ambassador Meets With Uzbekistan Minister of Investments, Industry, and Trade, Laziz Kudratov
incidents.description: During this meeting, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan discussed the status of bilateral trade and investment. Both agreed to increase mutual trade and investment.

incidents.title: Gas Prices Rise Across Central Asia
incidents.description: Amid recent Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, countries in Central Asia are facing rising energy prices and shortages. Tajikistan has reported increases in gas prices by 12% to 13%, Kyrgyzstan 10%, and Uzbekistan 11% to 11.5%. Meanwhile, Kazakhstan, despite meeting its own domestic demand, faces a fuel shortage as pressure mounts from neighboring markets.

incidents.title: Tajikistan, Turkmenistan Foreign Minister Meet for Consultations
incidents.description: Tajikistan and Turkmenistan's foreign ministers meet to discuss future cooperation between their states. Of particular focus were energy, transport, agriculture, and trade. No agreements were signed at this meeting.

incidents.title: Caspian States and Tajikistan Participate in Ferry Exercise
incidents.description: Customs officers from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan conducted an exercise aimed at streamlining the movement of passengers and cargo via the Caspian sea. The inclusion of Azerbaijan signals a growing effort by Central Asia to integrate that country into their economic and political community, similar to the New Lines S7+ framework.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan Added to China's 10 Day Visa-Free Transit Program
incidents.description: On August 20th, China's National Immigration Administration permitted Kazakhstan to join its 240-hour visa-free transit program. This permits Kyrgyz citizens to stay in China for up to 10 days without a visa, so long as they continue to a third country after their stop.

incidents.title: Turkmenistan, Tajikistan Foreign Ministers Discuss Areas of Future Cooperation
incidents.description: Foreign ministers met to discuss previous cooperation in trade and at the UN and how to expand trade and cooperation in energy, transport, agriculture, and humanitarian affairs.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan to Build 2nd Nuclear Plant with Russia
incidents.description: Uzbekistan President Mirziyoyev announced that Uzbekistan will build a 2d nuclear power plant, again with Russian assistance. Details of the plant remain sparse, and a formal deal with Russia still needs to be negotiated.

incidents.title: Amid Russian Fuel Shortages, Tajikistan Seeks Iranian OIl
incidents.description: While facing disruptions in Russian energy supply, Tajikistan has requested to purchase 2.55 million tons of crude oil and petroleum products from Iran.

incidents.title: Russian-Uzbek Agricultural Trade Up 31.7%
incidents.description: According to the Uzbek Ministry of Agriculture, trade turnover in agricultural products between Russia and Uzbekistan reached $1.55 billion from January to July 2026, a 31.7% increase compared with the same period last year.

incidents.title: Russia Reaffirms Commitment to Partnership with Turkmenistan
incidents.description: Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin sent a telegram to Turkmen President Serdar Berdimuhamedov, reaffirming Moscow’s commitment to expanding joint economic projects and strategic cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

incidents.title: Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan Ink $1bn Trade Goal, Tourism Agreement.
incidents.description: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan signed an agreement to deepen trade, with the ultimate goal of achieving $1bn in trade by 2030. To facilitate this goal, they established the Azerbaijan-Uzbekistan Investment Company to finance economic development. They also deepen cooperation in oil/gas exploration projects and to expand mutual tourism.

incidents.title: Russia, Tajikistan Expand Labor Migration Cooperation
incidents.description: Tajik officials signed cooperation agreements with several St. Petersburg employers and industry associations to expand organized employment opportunities in Russia for Tajik citizens.

incidents.title: Russia, Kazakhstan Announce Crude Processing Agreement
incidents.description: Kazakh Vice Minister of Energy Yerlan Akkenzhenov announced that the Kondensat refinery in western Kazakhstan will process Russian crude under a new bilateral agreement: 70% of the Kondensat refinery’s output will be exported to Russia, while the remaining 30% will serve the domestic market.

incidents.title: U.S. House Delegation Visits Uzbekistan in Support of Three-year Economic Cooperation Plan
incidents.description: A statement by Uzbek president Shavkat Mirziyoyev’s office following a meeting with a CODEL from the U.S. House of Representatives called for a further strengthening the strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and the United States in the areas of energy, critical minerals, transport, agriculture, and digital technologies. The Uzbek government claimed that bilateral trade has increased by 20% since the beginning of 2026, and highlighted the important role of the U.S. Congress in supporting reforms within Uzbekistan.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan's Embassy in Moscow Hosts Cultural Heritage Event
incidents.description: Collaborating with Russian travel agency Kaitan, the Embassy of Uzbekistan in Moscow hosted an event highlighting Uzbek tourism and cultural heritage. The event drew several Russian art and cultural figures in attendance and featured presentations on the history and tourism potential of Uzbekistan’s historical cities.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Transitions to Electronic Transport Permits for Russia, Belarus
incidents.description: Uzbekistan is working to digitize international road transport permits for Russia and Belarus by the end of 2026. Uzbekistan currently exchanges digital permits with six countries: Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, China, Turkey, Azerbaijan, and Georgia.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan Extends Fuel Import Subsidies
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan has extended its temporary fuel subsidy program through the end of 2026. These subsidies cover a portion of eligible importers’ fuel and transport costs when they exceed a fixed threshold. The extension also raised this price threshold, requiring importers to absorb a larger share of the cost before receiving state aid. This decision follows reports from Reuters on August 25 claiming Russia plans to extend its diesel export ban. Kyrgyzstan normally relies on Russia for over 90% of its imported fuel; however, Russian supplies are constrained by Ukrainian attacks on domestic refineries. Consequently, Kyrgyzstan aims to reduce its dependency on Russian energy and reduce the domestic impact of Russia’s oil shortage.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan Increases Berry Exports to Russia
incidents.description: From January 1 to August 25, Kyrgyz berry exports to Russia’s Kirov region surged by nearly 190% compared with the same period last year. Market experts attribute this increase to favorable weather conditions in Kyrgyzstan, stable logistics corridors, and expanded export channels. Additionally, retail prices for berries in the Kirov region have decreased by 15% to 25% year-on-year.

incidents.title: Tajikistan, China to Conduct Study on Feasibility of an AI Data Center
incidents.description: China and Tajikistan signed an agreement that allows China to conduct a feasibility analysis for a potential National Artificial Intelligence-Based Computing Center project in Tajikistan. If the study proves the project's viability, the two countries will sign a separate agreement to begin constructing the AI facility.

incidents.title: Turkmenistan's President Calls Kazakhstan's
incidents.description: Turkmenistan President Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedov spoke with Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomar Tokayev via phone call. Berdimuhamedov congratulated Tokayev on Kazakhstan's recent elections, and emphasized the growing cooperation on in AI.

incidents.title: Kyrgyz Tire Exports to Russia Surge Nearly 38-Fold
incidents.description: From January to June 2026, Kyrgyzstan’s tire exports to Russia increased by nearly 3,780% compared with the same period last year. Russia now absorbs 94.9% of Kyrgyzstan’s total tire exports.

incidents.title: Chinese President to Attend SCO Summit in Kyrgyzstan
incidents.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, alongside 20 other heads of state.

incidents.title: China-Uzbekistan Discuss Investment in Latter's Poultry Sector
incidents.description: Chinese corporate and Uzbekistani government representatives met to discuss possible Chinese investment in Uzbekistan's poultry sector. At the end of discussions, an agreement was signed where the Chinese Xinjiang Tycoon Group pledged to submit questions and information on proposed project to their Uzbekistani counterparts.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Signals Desire to Join US AI Initiative
incidents.description: Uzbekistan’s ambassador to the US, Furqat Sidikov, announced that the country has approached Washington about joining the US Pax Silica AI initiative, only a month after signing on to the Chinese World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. It was previously reported that the US had warned countries that membership in both agreements would not be allowed, so whether Uzbekistan is accepted into the US framework should be monitored.

incidents.title: Russia, China, Kazakhstan Seek Arctic Trade Corridor
incidents.description: Russia, China, and Kazakhstan are exploring a transport corridor along the Irtysh and Ob rivers. The route would reduce Chinese dependency on the Strait of Malacca, provide Kazakhstan with expanded inland shipping access, and give Russia an alternative shipping channel to bypass western sanctions.

incidents.title: China, Kazakhstan to Open First Ban Mo Training Center in Almaty
incidents.description: In partnership with China's Shandong University, Kazakhstan will establish its first Ban Mo workshop on Satbayev University's campus. Ban Mo is a Chinese technical education initiative that trains engineering students to work with modern equipment. The program aims to develop a workforce of local operators knowledgeable about Chinese manufacturing and equipment.

incidents.title: Kyrgyz and Chinese Presidents Sign 30 Joint Documents
incidents.description: On August 31, Kyrgyzstan and China signed 30 agreements, memorandums, and joint protocols covering multiple industries and areas of cooperation. Key agreements included the Treaty on Eternal Good-Neighborliness and the Joint Declaration of Kyrgyzstan and China on the High-Quality Development of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in the New Era, both of which were signed by the heads of state.

incidents.title: Russia Mandates Mobile Registration App for Visa-Free Foreigners
incidents.description: Effective September 1, Russia will require all adult foreign nationals entering on a visa-free basis, including Tajik citizens, to register via the mobile application “Amina”. The app obligates foreign nationals to report information about their place of residence to Russian authorities.

incidents.title: US Senator and Special Envoy Meet with Tajik President Before Chinese Summit
incidents.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon met with US Special Presidential Envoy for Central and South Asia Sergio Gor and Senator Steve Daines in Bishkek on August 31. The two sides discussed various issues of bilateral economic and governmental cooperation. The meeting comes days before the Tajik leader journeys to Bishkek to attend China’s SCO economic summit.

incidents.title: Russia, Uzbekistan Discuss Joint Projects
incidents.description: Uzbek Deputy Prime Minister Jamshid Khodjaev met with Russian Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade Alexey Gruzdev to discuss bilateral trade and joint projects in energy, geology, chemicals, transport, logistics, agriculture, and construction.

incidents.title: Russia, Uzbekistan Discuss Migrant Protections
incidents.description: Russian and Uzbek officials convened in Moscow to discuss legal protections and rights for Uzbek citizens residing in Russia.

incidents.title: Official Footage Confirms Uzbekistan's Use of Chinese Fighter Jets
incidents.description: Uzbekistan's defense ministry released official footage of Chinese J-10CE fighter jets, making Uzbekistan the second confirmed non-Chinese operator of this aircraft, following Pakistan. While Uzbekistan has primarily used Soviet-designed jets for the past 30 years, acquiring the J-10CE diversifies its military aircraft sourcing.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Designated Compliant with US Fiscal Transparency Requirements
incidents.description: In 2025, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan were the only Central Asian countries to meet the US State Department’s minimum fiscal transparency requirements, according to the recently released 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report. No other Central Asian states made “significant progress” during the review period.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan Designated Compliant with US Fiscal Transparency Requirements
incidents.description: In 2025, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan were the only Central Asian countries to meet the US State Department’s minimum fiscal transparency requirements, according to the recently released 2026 Fiscal Transparency Report. No other Central Asian states made “significant progress” during the review period.

incidents.title: US Officials Crash SCO Summit
incidents.description: Two high-level US officials, special presidential envoy Sergio Gor and Republican Senator Steve Daines, arrived uninvited to the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, weakening the portrait of unity among the gathered countries. Though they didn’t participate in any SCO-sanctioned events, Gor and Daines held one-on-one meetings with the presidents of Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan, in the hope of deepening US ties with the region.

incidents.title: Chinese Airline to Operate Four Weekly Cargo Flights from Kazakhstan
incidents.description: China Central Longhao, a Chinese cargo airline, will begin operating four weekly flights from Astana International Airport in Kazakhstan in September. This is expected to further position Astana as a city connecting Chinese, Central Asian, and international trade.

incidents.title: Utah Men Represent US at Kyrgyz Nomad Games
incidents.description: Five men from Utah participated in the kok-boru event at the “Nomad Games” in Bishkek. Kok-boru competitors pass a goat carcass between teammates on horseback, scoring by throwing the goat into the opposing team's goal. It's the official national equestrian sport of Kyrgyzstan, which hosted the games from 8/31 to 9/6. Both John Fosgren of Cornisha and Brian Ewell of Genola stated that it was an honor to represent the United States at the event.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Opens Seattle Consulate, with More Planned Across US
incidents.description: Uzbekistan has opened a new consulate general in Seattle, WA, part of a broader initiative instituted by an Uzbek presidential decree to expand the country’s diplomatic presence across the United States. Uzbek officials plan to use the new consulate to promote business partnerships with U.S companies and foreign investment into Central Asia. Similar consulates are planned for the cities of Chicago, Philadelphia, and Orlando.

incidents.title: Key Tunnel Successfully Drilled in CKU Railway Project
incidents.description: Project officials of the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan (CKU) railway announced that they have successfully drilled a key tunnel in Kyrgyzstan, marking a significant milestone in the completion of this long-awaited railway project. Once completed, the CKU railway will be the shortest overland corridor between China, the Middle East, and Europe, allowing trade between China and these regions to circumvent Russia.

incidents.title: China Urges Central Asian Security Forces to Safeguard Joint Economic and Strategic Interests
incidents.description: During an informal meeting in Beijing, Chinese Public Security Minister Wang Xiaohong urged security forces from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan to jointly counter terrorism, extremism, and separatism. This meeting occurred amid China's ongoing expansion of trade and energy routes throughout Central Asia, which are key to the country's strategic and economic interests.

incidents.title: China, Kazakhstan to Reciprocally Recognize National Drivers Licenses
incidents.description: Following a meeting in Beijing between Kazakhstan’s Interior Minister Yerzhan Sadenov and China’s Minister of Public Security Wang Xiaohong, China and Kazakhstan will recognize each other's national driver's licenses, which Kazakhstan's ministry indicated would streamline cross-border travel processes.

incidents.title: Congressman Proposes Trade Liberalization with Kazakhstan
incidents.description: Democratic Congressman Jimmy Panetta stated at a Hudson Institute discussion that repealing the Cold War-era Jackson-Vanik amendment, which currently restricts US-Kazakh trade relations, would serve Washington’s critical mineral and supply chain interests in Central Asia. His comments followed a recent House Ways and Means Committee hearing on the issue.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Expand Interior Ministry Offices
incidents.description: Russia and Kyrgyzstan have signed an agreement expanding their respective Interior Ministry offices. Russia’s office in Bishkek will handle broader law enforcement matters and engage in direct information sharing with Kyrgyz authorities. Meanwhile, Kyrgyzstan will establish a dedicated Interior Ministry office in Moscow; its existing migration office will be converted into a representative office for its Ministry of Labor, Social Security and Migration.

incidents.title: Russia Emphasizes Tajik-Afghan Border Security
incidents.description: During a ceremony marking the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan’s independence, Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov stated that securing Tajikistan’s border with Afghanistan remains a priority for Moscow. Dushanbe has raised concerns over security risks along its 1300-kilometer border with Afghanistan in recent months ,and Russia has repeatedly warned of potential instability and spillover from terrorist groups in the region.

incidents.title: Russia, Turkmenistan Discuss Trade, Joint Ventures
incidents.description: St. Petersburg Governor Alexander Beglov met with Turkmen officials during a working visit to Turkmenistan to discuss trade in pharmaceutical products and equipment supply for new international medical centers in Ashgabat.

incidents.title: Chinese Energy Corporation to Invest $1.2 Billion in Kazakh Wind Farms
incidents.description: According to Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry, Chinese energy company State Power Investment Corporation will invest $1.2 billion in the construction of a wind farm near Ekibastuz, Kazakhstan. The farm is expected to being operating in 2029.

incidents.title: Uzbek Court Sentences Citizen for Joining Russia's War in Ukraine
incidents.description: An Uzbek court has sentenced a 25-year-old citizen to two years in prison for fighting alongside Russian forces in Ukraine. The man migrated to Russia for work in November 2021 and was arrested on drug charges in October 2023. While serving his sentence, he was offered release, financial compensation, and Russian citizenship in exchange for military service. He reported that after initially refusing, prison authorities coerced inmates through intimidation, solitary confinement, and torture.

incidents.title: Russia, Uzbekistan Increase Railway Digitalization
incidents.description: Russia’s TransTeleSoft and Uzbekistan’s Tashkent State Transport University will establish a long-term partnership across education, research, and industry to develop and support onboard systems for railway rolling stock.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Agrees to Participate in EAEU Cooperation Projects
incidents.description: Kazakhstan agreed to participate in a series of EAEU cooperation projects in the agricultural and construction sector. These projects will benefit from more generous financing terms and accelerated permitting processes. Also agreed at this meeting were common safety standards for the production of toys.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce QR Payments in China
incidents.description: Kazakhstan is working to introduce a cross-border payment service in China by the end of 2026 that would allow Kazakh citizens to use their usual banking apps abroad after scanning a QR code.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan to Build $100 Million Logistics Center Near Chinese Border
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan's National Investment Agency signed a memorandum with Kyrgyz company Textile Trans to build a $100 million logistics center at the Kyrgyzstan-China border, intended to facilitate flows of Chinese goods through Uzbekistan and Afghanistan toward Pakistan. The new logistics center would also expand Kyrgyzstan's access to South Asian ports, as trade between Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan remains limited.

incidents.title: China, Uzbekistan to issue $250 million of bonds on Hong Kong Stock Exchange
incidents.description: The National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity of the Republic of Uzbekistan (UzNB) and China International Capital Corporation (CICC) plan to jointly issue $250 million worth of bonds in both China's and Uzbekistan's respective currencies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, allowing Uzbekistan to enter the Asian financial markets, attract international investors, and diversify its currency exposure.

incidents.title: Kazakh President Receives Personal Message from Trump via Special Envoy Gor
incidents.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with U.S. Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor tangentially to the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He passed along a personal message from President Donald Trump that congratulated the Kazakh nation on its upcoming 35th anniversary of independence. Tokayev stated that his attendance at the G20 Summit in December would allow the two heads of state to discuss high-priority areas of cooperation, particularly artificial intelligence and digitalization.

incidents.title: Russia Surpasses Kazakhstan as Kyrgyzstan's Top Wheat Supplier
incidents.description: From January to June 2026, Kyrgyz wheat imports from Russia grew 4.8-fold, year-on-year. Meanwhile, imports from Kazakhstan—traditionally Kyrgyzstan’s primary grain supplier—fell nearly 50%.

incidents.title: China, Uzbekistan Sign Memorandum To Build Water Treatment Plant in Navoi
incidents.description: State-owned Uzbek water management company JSC Uzsuvtaminot signed a memorandum of understanding with China Energy Overseas Investment Co., Ltd. to increase water resource and sanitation coordination in Uzbekistan. One goal of expanding water resource cooperation is to establish Uzbekistan's first large drinking water treatment plant in Navoi using nanofiltration technologies. The practical and technical implementation processes required to build this facility were discussed at the signing of this memorandum.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan Deputy Transport Ministers Discuss Areas for Cooperation
incidents.description: At a meeting between First Deputy Minister of Transport of Uzbekistan Mamanbiy Omarov and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Republic of Kazakhstan Maksat Kaliakparov, expanding and improving cross-border trade were discussed. Particular focus was on improving the quality of international roads, as well as making permitting systems more efficient.

incidents.title: Russia, Kazakhstan Expand Gas Supply Contract
incidents.description: Russia’s Gazprom has signed a supplementary agreement extending its gas supply contract with Kazakhstan. The parties plan to finalize a long-term agreement by 2027.

incidents.title: Central Asian States Look to Strengthen Expert Food Quality
incidents.description: At Kyrgyzstan's request, Central Asian states and the United Nations Development Programme are putting a workshop to share best practices for aligning agricultural projects with international export standards.

incidents.title: US and Uzbekistan Conclude Joint Cultural Heritage Workshops
incidents.description: On Sep 16th, the United States Embassy in Uzbekistan announced the completion of a series of joint workshops in Tashkent and Samarkand in May 2026, which focused on the protection of Uzbekistan’s cultural heritage. The workshops are part of a longer-term U.S.-Uzbek commitment to guarding cultural heritage established by the 2023 Cultural Property Agreement.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan Friendship Canal is Concreted
incidents.description: To strengthen the walls of a cross border canal between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, Uzbekistan began concreting a 3.4-kilometer section. This is important for preventing water loss through filtration. The total cost of this project will be 77.2 billion Uzbek soums (~$6,532,000)

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Foreign Minister Hosts Kyrgyzstan Ambassador
incidents.description: During their meeting Kazakhstan's Foreign minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi spoke with Kyrgyz Ambassador Kudaibergen Bazarbaev discussed current issues facing their countries' bilateral relations and how to enhance cooperation between their countries in the realm of trade (especially water and energy). No agreements were signed between these states.

incidents.title: Russia, Kazakhstan Convene on Irtysh River, Seek Chinese Participation
incidents.description: A joint Russian-Kazakh working group has prepared a plan to improve water and environmental security and develop energy infrastructure along the Irtysh River. Russian Minister of Natural Resources and Environment Alexander Kozlov stated that the group is exploring trilateral consultations on Irtysh management with Beijing.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Rises 11% in 2025
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan’s economy grew by 11% in 2025. According to the Asian Development Bank, re-exporting goods to Russia accounted for 30-40% of growth over the past four years. Other drivers include surging gold prices, a growing crypto and finance sector, and increased public spending on construction.

incidents.title: Costco Executives Discuss Produce Imports from Uzbekistan
incidents.description: Costco is considering adding Uzbek fruits and vegetables to its shelves after a meeting in September with Akhror Burkhonov, head of the Uzbek Consulate in Seattle, according to reports from state media. Plans were drafted for Uzbek suppliers to give product presentations to Costco procurement officials in February 2027, representing an emerging shift away from the traditional Uzbek agricultural export markets of Russia and China.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan, Russia Discuss Nuclear Safety
incidents.description: On the sidelines of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s 70th General Conference, Uzbek Committee for Industrial, Radiation, and Nuclear Safety officials met with a Russian delegation to discuss radiation safety, nuclear regulation, licensing, inspection protocols, and bilateral cooperation. The meeting aimed to support Uzbekistan’s national nuclear safety architecture.

incidents.title: Russia, Uzbekistan Establish Anti-Corruption Program for 2027-2028
incidents.description: Russia and Uzbekistan signed a bilateral program covering 2027-2028 that aims to strengthen joint cooperation in combating corruption. The program will focus on sharing preventative measures, using digital tools to identify corruption risks, building institutional transparency, and advancing scientific and educational cooperation.

incidents.title: Tajikistani Ambassador Discusses Economic Cooperation with US Assistant Treasury Secretary
incidents.description: Tajikistan’s Ambassador to the US Zavqi Zavqizoda and US Assistant Secretary of the Treasury Jeremy Wiggins met and discussed prospects for economic and financial cooperation on September 17th. Few details about the meeting were released.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Plan Joint Ventures in Fishing Industry
incidents.description: During the 11th International Fishery Forum in St. Petersburg, officials from Russia and Kyrgyzstan discussed plans to expand bilateral cooperation in the fishing industry.

incidents.title: Montana National Guard Completes 30th Year of Training with Kyrgyz Military
incidents.description: Soldiers of the US Air Force and the Montana National Guard recently completed the “Ak Shumkar II” exercise alongside the Kyrgyz military. The training program focused on disaster response, fire and rescue operations, and urban search and rescue, and represented the 30th year of partnership between Montana and the Kyrgyz Republic via the DoW National Guard Bureau State Partnership Program.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Moves Closer to US on Issue of Nuclear Safety
incidents.description: US and Uzbek officials signed an MOU on safe operations and disaster response on the sidelines of the International Atomic Energy Agency general conference in Vienna. The memo allows for US technical assistance in “the peaceful use of nuclear energy,” according to the Uzbek Committee on Industrial, Radiation and Nuclear Safety. Uzbek officials also held talks with their Russian counterparts at the IAEA event, but no memos or agreements came out of the meeting, potentially signaling a shift away from Russian influence in the realm of nuclear energy.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan Develops Anti-Inflation Plan
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan’s Ministry of Economy and Commerce drafted an action plan to stabilize inflation, which reached 12% last month. The plan aims to increase agricultural imports from Russia, Kazakhstan, and Belarus and extend fuel subsidies.

incidents.title: Kazakh President Meets with US Businesses During UNGA Visit
incidents.description: Kazakhstani President Erzhan Kazykhan met with US business leaders at an event co-hosted by the Embassy of Kazakhstan and the Atlantic Council in the days before the UN General Assembly in New York. Discussions centered on Kazakhstan’s integration into global value chains and cooperation with the United States on AI and critical minerals, including uranium.

incidents.title: Kyrgyz President Visits Nomad Games Athlete in Utah Before UNGA, Signs Transport Deal with US Company
incidents.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov stopped in Utah on his journey to New York for the UNGA and met with Ladd Howell, captain of the U.S. kok-boru team at World Nomad Games, held last month in Kyrgyzstan. Howell presented Japarov with his Team USA jersey and cowboy hat. On his way to NY, Japarov also met executives from American locomotive maker Wabtec, signing a contract for 10 freight locomotives for Kyrgyzstan’s state-owned railway company. Additional meetings were held with the StoneX Group and Citibank.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan Hosts Trilateral Talks on Kambarata Hydropower Project
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan, hosted delegates from Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan to discuss the implementation terms for the Kambarata-1 hydropower project. This proposed hydroelectric plant would harness energy from the Naryn River in Kyrgyzstan and would provide electricity to the other parties to this agreement.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan Meet to Discuss Border Security
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan representative met to discuss how to enhance cooperation between each other's border security. They will also exchange best practices with one another and negotiate how to increase direct communication between border agencies.

incidents.title: CSTO Foreign Ministers Meet on UNGA Sideline
incidents.description: During the 2026 United Nations General Assembly, Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) foreign ministers discussed possible areas of cooperation in the UN system. At the end, all parties reaffirmed a commitment to strengthening the relevancy of the CSTO in the international system.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Plans Nationwide Storage Systems
incidents.description: According to Uzbek Energy Minister Sherwood Khojaev, a meeting chaired by President Shavkat MIrziyoyev reviewed projects in the power sector to increase electricity generation at a pace corresponding to GDP growth in order to meet the needs of Uzbekistan’s population and economy. The meeting’s main focus was on establishing storage systems throughout the country, enhancing the investment selection and planning process, and expanding the state’s solar and wind generation capacities. This comes during a period of high energy costs due to Russia’s oil shortage, which underscores the urgency behind Uzbekistan’s diversification efforts.

incidents.title: Secretary Rubio to Lead Delegation to Uzbekistan Summit
incidents.description: Special Envoy Central Asia Sergio Gor announced that Secretary of State Marco Rubio will lead a delegation of dozens of American companies to Uzbekistan in mid-October, taking part in the C5+1 Ministerial summit with the foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. Discussions with the Uzbek government will focus on trade expansion, private-sector investment, and economic modernization across the region.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan-China Investment Forum Yields 10 Signed Agreements
incidents.description: During the Kazakhstan-China investment forum held in Almaty, Kazakhstani and Chinese companies signed 10 agreements to finance and build new projects in Kazakhstan, covering automotive manufacturing, fertilizer production, and AI/tech developments.

incidents.title: President Trump Appoints New Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan
incidents.description: President Trump nominated career diplomat Stephen Gillen as the United States Ambassador to Kyrgyzstan, and his candidacy is awaiting Senate approval. Gillen served as Deputy Special Representative of the US President for Hostage Affairs from 2021 to 2024, and has extensive experience working in US embassies (Belarus, Iraq, Bosnia and Herzegovina). The nomination comes as US Ambassador Leslie Vigieri’s term concludes.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Explores New Caspian Energy Route Bypassing Russia
incidents.description: A working group representing eight Kazakh oil shareholders agreed to a feasibility study for an alternative oil pipeline route. The plan would move oil from Atryau to Aktau, Kazakhstan, across the Caspian Sea to Baku, connecting to the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline. This comes amid frequent disruptions to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) due to Ukrainian drone strikes. The working group is considering a subsea pipeline or large tanker fleet that could eventually handle 35 million metric tons of oil annually, more than 30 times Kazakhstan’s current volume of shipments across the Caspian.

incidents.title: State Department Official Visits Existing Investment Initiatives During Astana Conference
incidents.description: At the C5+1 Conference in Astana on September 29, Mark Cameron, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Central Asian Affairs and Public Diplomacy at the US Department of State, highlighted successes of the current period of US engagement with Central Asia and Kazakhstan. Cameron announced that he would visit existing initiatives in the region during his next two days in Astana.

incidents.title: FAA Visits Astana to Judge Government and Private Sector Compliance
incidents.description: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) completed an International Aviation Safety Assessment (IASA) of Kazakhstan’s aviation safety system last week, according to the Kazakh Civil Aviation Committee’s press service. The FAA officials reviewed Kazakhstan’s aviation legislation implementation and the country’s capacity to exercise effective aviation safety operations. The FAA team also visited Air Astana headquarters, a company that is applying for authorization from the U.S. Department of Transportation to fly in US airspace. According to Kazakh officials, the tenor of the visit was positive and productive.

incidents.title: Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan sign Data Sharing Agreement
incidents.description: Attorney generals from Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan have signed an agreement to share information on “terrorist and extremist organizations, groups, and individuals” that pose “a threat to the security of states”.

incidents.title: Kyrgyz Investment Head Visits Turkmenistan
incidents.description: Ravshanbek Sabirov, head of Kyrgyz Republic's National Investment Agency, vitied Turkmenistan to discuss how to increase economic trade, with a particular focus on oil and gas. No agreements were signed, however both parties agreed to continue talks in the future.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan Discuss Future Roadmap for Trade
incidents.description: Kazakhstan Deputy Prime Minister and National Economy Minister Serik Zhumangarin and Deputy Prime Minister of Uzbekistan Jamshid Khodjaev met in Astana to discuss progress in deepening trade between states and to establish a road map for expanding trade in 2027.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Increases Gas Imports from Russia, Turkmenistan
incidents.description: Between January and August 2026, Uzbekistan’s natural gas imports from Russia and Turkmenistan increased by 15.2%.

incidents.title: Money Transfers Between Russia, Kazakhstan Fall 12-fold
incidents.description: In August, the value of money transfers from Russia to Kazakhstan fell nearly 12-fold, while transfers from from Kazakhstan to Russia dropped over 14-fold . This comes after the EU imposed sanctions on the Zolotaya Korona payment system in late July.

incidents.title: Head of Uzbek Presidential Administration Meets with Trump in DC
incidents.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, met with President Trump in DC on behalf of Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Mirziyoyeva additionally holds the position of co-chair of the American-Uzbek Business and Investment Council, which seeks to strengthen investment and business ties between the US and the Central Asian state.

incidents.title: Uzbek Embassy Hosts Business Forum in DC
incidents.description: The first-ever Uzbek-American Transport and Logistics Forum, hosted by the Embassy of Uzbekistan to the United States and “IT Park Uzbekistan,” took place in Washington, DC, involving leaders from over 70 transport and logistics companies run by Uzbek citizens that pursue business operations in the US. The US market accounts for 54% of the total export volume from “IT Park Uzbekistan” companies.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Increases Grain Exports to China, Afghanistan
incidents.description: In September 2026, Kazakhstan more than doubled its grain exports by rail to China, and more than tripled its rail exports of grain to Afghanistan compared to September 2025.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Sign Agreement on Combating Drug Trafficking
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan’s Minister of Internal Affairs Ulan Niyazbekov has signed a cooperation agreement with Russia’s Minister of Internal Affairs Vladimir Kolokoltsev on combating illicit drug trafficking. The agreement is effective through 2028 and focuses on joint efforts to stop the illegal transit and trafficking of narcotics between Russia and Kyrgyzstan.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Discuss Education of Kyrgyz Children in Russia
incidents.description: Kyrgyz Deputy Minister of Education Nadira Dzhusupbekova met with Russian Deputy Head of Rossotrudnichestvo Natalia Kiseleva to discuss improving mechanisms for the preparing and taking of entrance tests for Kyrgyz children seeking admission to Russian educational institutions.

incidents.title: Seven OPEC+ Countries Review Global Market Conditions and Outlook
incidents.description: Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman met virtually to review market conditions and outlook. During the meeting, the parties decided to maintain September 2026 production quotas for November 2026 and reaffirmed their collective commitment to achieve full conformity with the Declaration of Cooperation. The next meeting is scheduled for November 1, 2026.

incidents.title: Special Envoy Teases Trump Visit to Uzbekistan, Air Transport Expansion
incidents.description: Paolo Zampolli, US Special Envoy for Global Partnerships and personal friend of Donald Trump, told an Uzbek television interviewer during a visit to the country that Uzbekistan is on Trump’s presidential visit “to-do” list, citing his strong personal bond with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. During his visit, Zampolli also pointed out US support for Uzbekistan's attempt to become a regional flight hub. A recent Boeing forecast marked Central Asia as a top market for airline growth opportunities in the coming decades.

incidents.title: Kyrgyzstan, Russia Establish Legal Assistance Center
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan and Russia will establish a bilateral legal assistance center for their citizens. The center intends to help Kyrgyz citizens in Russia and Russian citizens in Kyrgyzstan obtain documents and resolve social and legal issues.

incidents.title: Russia, Kazakhstan Convene on Joint Use of Water Resources
incidents.description: The Kazakhstan-Russia Joint Commission on the Use and Protection of Transboundary Water Resources held its 16th meeting in Yekaterinburg, Russia where the sides discussed issues related to managing spring floods, filling reservoirs, and ensuring water supplies for the population and economic sectors. Officials also reviewed the results of state monitoring of transboundary water resources and ongoing water protection measures.

incidents.title: Russia, Uzbekistan Expand Cultural Cooperation for 2027-2029
incidents.description: During a meeting at the Days of Culture of Uzbekistan in Russia, Russia’s Culture Minister Olga Lyubimova Uzbekistan’s Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to Russia Botirjon Asadov signed a memorandum expanding cooperation in education, implementation of creative projects, experience sharing , and cooperation between specialists and students.

incidents.title: Russia Remains Largest Labor Market for Central Asian States
incidents.description: According to the Director of the Third Department of the CIS Countries at the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs Alexander Sternik, Russia remains the largest labor market for citizens of the Central Asian states, despite a slight decline in labor migrants to Russia.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Compiles List of Citizens in Ukraine War Zone for Transfer to Russia
incidents.description: Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said negotiations are underway for the repatriation of its citizens in the war zone in Ukraine. The Ministry is compiling information on each citizen who has inquired via their hotline services and will send the list to Russia once completed.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan, Russia Deepen Joint Projects During 3rd meeting of the Council of Regions
incidents.description: Representatives from all regions of Uzbekistan, 17 Russian regions, and approximately 400 entrepreneurs from both countries attended the 3rd meeting of the Council of Regions in Fergana, Uzbekistan. The meeting discussed expanding industrial cooperation, trade, investment, and joint projects between the two countries whose bilateral portfolio includes over 200 projects worth nearly $6 billion. Four agreements were signed during the meeting: (1) the Fergana Region and Omsk Region signed an agreement on industrial cooperation; (2) Surkhandarya Region and Kranoyarsk Krai signed an agreement on cooperation in trade, economic, scientific, technical, cultural, and humanitarian spheres; (3) the Namangan Region and Dagestan agreed on an action plan to implement the agreement on trade, economic, scientific, technical, and socio-cultural cooperation; (4) Wildberries signed an agreement with the Ministry of Investment, Industry, and Trade to develop a Class A logistics complex.

incidents.title: Suspected Russian Plague Prompts Health Checks Across Central Asia
incidents.description: The death of an employee who accidentally broke a test tube containing live bacteria at an anti-plague research institute in Russia’s Irkutsk region has prompted health authorities in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan to tighten sanitary controls and review preparedness measures. Nearly 200 people who might have come into contact with the employee are under medical observation; four hospitals are under quarantine with approximately 100 people hospitalized as a precaution. Russian officials say there is no reason for alarm—health specialists are investigating and have urged the public not to speculate before an official assessment of the situation is released. Though risk of exposure is low, Kazakhstan’s Health Ministry said it was aware of the situation and had ordered sanitary and quarantine checks at border crossings and other entry points. Kyrgyzstan’s Health Ministry has also stepped up preventative measures, with specialists monitoring individuals, vehicles, and cargo at border crossings. Tajikistan’s Health Ministry has ordered that individuals crossing into the country have their body temperature measured and are asked whether they are experiencing symptoms such as nausea and vomiting, headache, weakness, and muscle and joint pain. Personnel have also been instructed to wear disposable hazmat clothing when working at entry points. Uzbekistan’s Committee for Sanitary and Epidemiological Welfare and Public Health said it is closely monitoring the situation and has increased the preparedness of relevant services to prevent the introduction and spread of highly infectious diseases within the country. Turkmenistan has not commented on the situation.

incidents.title: Department of Energy Help Kazakhstan Open Radiation Monitoring Center
incidents.description: Kazakhstan opened a new center for radiation monitoring on October 2 with the support of the US Department of Energy’s National Nuclear Security Administration, as the country works to develop domestic nuclear energy infrastructure. The facility will help the country avoid negative impacts resulting from the legacy of USSR nuclear testing on its territory.

incidents.title: US Provides Counterterrorism UAVs to Tajik Border Guards
incidents.description: The United States Embassy in Dushanbe announced that the US has provided six border security UAVs worth $2.3 million to Tajikistan’s National Guard, which will be used for surveillance and counterterrorism operations. They are part of $600 million in security assistance provided to Tajikistan since its independence.

incidents.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Briefed on Russian Company LUKOIL's Activities
incidents.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with Vagit Alekperov—founder of Russian oil company LUKOIL. LUKOIL holds stakes in several oil and gas projects in Kazakhstan. Alekperov briefed Tokayev on the current state of LUKOIL’s projects in Kazakhstan and discussed further development of frameworks for their joint projects in the oil and gas sectors.

incidents.title: Russia, Kazakhstan Extend Oil Supply Agreement Until 2028
incidents.description: Kazakhstan is extending its agreement with Russia until January 1, 2028. The agreement preserves the existing mechanism for supply coordination and information exchange while maintaining the possibility of resuming duty-free imports of petrol products. Kazakhstan’s Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov said the agreement is important for the country’s energy security and stability of its domestic supply.

incidents.title: Russia’s Wildberries to Build New Logistics Hub in Uzbekistan
incidents.description: Wildberries & Russ has signed an investment agreement with Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Investment, Industry, and Trade to construct a modern, multi-industry logistics complex located on a 67.3-hectare site in the Zangiata district of the Tashkent region. Wildberries aims to create a minimum of 7,500 jobs at the complex and commit at least 2,000 to training in specialized educational programs. This comes after Wildberries’ CEO Robert Mirzoyan announced, in June, the company’s plans to invest over $300 million in the Uzbek economy.

incidents.title: Azerbaijan, Central Asian States Meet to Discuss Future Cooperation
incidents.description: Central Asian states and Azerbaijan met in Turkmenistan to layout a roadmap for future cooperation. At the conclusion of the meetings, a draft agenda for future negotiations was agreed to.

incidents.title: Turkmenistan President Hosts Kyrgyz Counterpart
incidents.description: Turkmenistan President Serdar Berdimuhmedov hosted Kyrgyz Republic President Sadyr Japarov at a summit meeting where they discussed how to expand trade, economic, transportation, and energy cooperation. While no agreements were signed, both expressed optimism that future negotiations would bare fruit.

incidents.title: Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan Establish Supreme Council of Strategic Partnership
incidents.description: Turkmenistan President Serdar Berdimuhamedov and Uzbekistan President Shavket Mirziyuoyev signed an agreement to establish the Supreme Council of Strategic Partnership. This body will develop new ways to deepen their bilateral relations. The also discussed the adoption of an action plan to increase trade and industrial, energy, transport, water, and agricultural cooperation.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, and Tajikistan Representatives Gather in Azava National Tourist Zone to Discuss Water Management
incidents.description: Representatives of Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kazakhstan, and Tajikistan met to discuss the management of shared water resources. At the conclusion of the meeting, an agreement to regulate withdrawal limits for the Amu Darya and Syr Karya was reached.

incidents.title: Merger between US and Uzbek Companies Completed
incidents.description: TEG LLC, an Uzbekistan-based tourism and events business, announced the successful completion of its merger with US company StageWise Strategies Corp., creating the first U.S.- traded Uzbekistan-based business. The US company will operate as TEG Overseas, Inc.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan Expands Digital Transport Permits with Turkic States
incidents.description: Kazakhstan's Chairman for Road Transport and Transport Control, Dastan Zhumakulov, announced that Kazakhstan will continue to expand digital permits for cross border freight coming from and to Azerbaijan, Georgia, Turkiye, and Kyrgyzstan. This year, Kazakhstan granted 700,000 permits. The digitization of cross border transports reduces administrative obstacles, allowing for more efficient cross border trade.

incidents.title: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan Aim to Enhance Middle Corridor Transport
incidents.description: During the New Silk Way Business Forum in Kazakhstan, representatives from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan's transportation ministries and sectors discussed different proposals to enhance railway infrastructure and logistics services, including digitizing permits and information exchanges.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan Discuss Expanded Agricultural and Industrial Cooperation
incidents.description: Representatives of Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan discussed various cooperation proposals in industry and agriculture. While no state to state agreements were signed, they agreed to continue talks and to encourage business-to-business negotiations.

incidents.title: Central Asian Green Energy Corridor Established
incidents.description: Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, and Uzbekistan have signed a strategic partnership to increase green energy production and supply across Central Asian borders. Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev also discussed proposals to increase trans-Caspian oil transportation.

incidents.title: Tajikistan to Ease Rules for Joint Investments with Uzbekistan
incidents.description: Tajikistan will reform the Tajik-Uzbek Investment Company's operating rules to allow the use of foreign currency and streamline project financing mechanisms. Of particular emphasis was authorizing lease financing for industrial equipment.

incidents.title: Central Asian & Caucasian States Sign Protocol to Expand CASCA+
incidents.description: Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Turkey have signed a an agreement to increase cargo volumes, reduce tariffs, and streamline logistics along the CASCA+ corridor. This corridor, launched in 2019, serves to increase Central Asian trade with Europe.

incidents.title: Central Asian Summit Includes Azerbaijan, See Renewed Calls for Regional Integration
incidents.description: At the 8th Consultative Meeting of the Hds of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan heads of states discussed issues facing Central Asian trade. Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted that trade between Central Asian states account for only 8% of their combined trade turnover, with most trade going to countries outside the region. He proposed to his colleagues that states bring trade, water, and logistics into a common framework. Also noteworthy, is this is Azerbaijan's first time participating as a full member of the grouping.

incidents.title: Turkmenistan Hosts Central Asian Meeting of Education Ministry Representatives
incidents.description: At a meeting of the DARYA Project High-Level Group in Ashgabat, representatives of Central Asian education ministries discussed the need to establish mutual recognition of professional qualifications. No agreements were signed.

incidents.title: Kazakhstan, Tajikistan Agree to Expand Rail Cargo Cooperation
incidents.description: Kazakhstan and Tajikistan discussed obstacles to cross border logistics. Following deliberations, they signed a protocol established 100 billion tons by 2034 as a target.

incidents.title: Tajikistan Signs MOU with Chinese Hydropower Firm
incidents.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy and Water Resources signed a memorandum of understanding with Xinjiang Shouhai Power Development Co., to assess the Obihingou River's hydroelectric potential. The current project output potential estimate is 2,610 MW, which would make it one of the largest sources of energy in Tajikistan.

incidents.title: Proposed Mining Company Merger Opens Kazakhstan's Tungsten Business to US
incidents.description: Skyline Builders Group Holding Limited reported on Oct. 12, in an effort to garner financial support from Washington, that its proposed merger with Cove Kaz Capital Group LLC would lead to two major tungsten deposits in Kazakhstan coming under US supply-chain control. Cove Kaz is a mineral developer currently working with Kazakhstan's national mining company, Tau-Ken Samruk. According to the companies, the US government is considering a potential $1.6 billion in financing for the project, which would provide critical mineral access in a country largely enmeshed in the Chinese economic sphere.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Capital Market Reforms with US Firm Franklin Templeton
incidents.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Jamshid Kuchkarov met representatives of Franklin Templeton to discuss state-owned enterprise reform, improving corporate governance and transparency, preparations for potential initial public offerings, and access to international capital markets. The parties expressed interest in maintaining dialogue and exploring possible joint initiatives; no new binding agreement was reported.

incidents.title: US Ambassador Discusses Logistics Cooperation at Turkmenbashi Port
incidents.description: The US ambassador to Turkmenistan met with leaders of the Turkmenbashi International Seaport to discuss regional security, transport corridors between Asia and Europe, and opportunities to expand multimodal freight logistics. The US side expressed interest in the port's capacity and in introducing American technology and expertise. No formal agreement was announced.

incidents.title: Uzbek President Meets US Special Envoy Ahead of C5+1 Ministerial
incidents.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met US Special Envoy Sergio Gor to discuss preparations for Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit, the C5+1 ministerial, and the second Uzbekistan–US Business and Investment Council meeting. They emphasized developing investment proposals and implementing joint projects but reported no new agreement at this meeting.

incidents.title: United States and Central Asian Foreign Ministers Adopt C5+1 Joint Statement
incidents.description: The US Secretary of State and foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan adopted a C5+1 joint statement in Samarkand. The document sets shared priorities for the Trans-Caspian trade route, regional customs and logistics integration, critical-mineral extraction and processing, energy cooperation, cybersecurity, border security, and educational exchanges. The statement outlines intended cooperation rather than project-specific financing.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan and US Businesses Announce 54 Agreements Worth Up to $12 Billion
incidents.description: During the Uzbekistan–US Business and Investment Council meeting in Samarkand, officials announced 54 agreements covering projects that would total approximately $12 billion if implemented. The package covers railway equipment localization with Wabtec, aircraft engines from GE Aerospace, finance with US firms, critical-mineral activities with ReElement Technologies and others, and projects in satellite communications, healthcare, and agriculture. The announced amount is prospective and does not represent confirmed disbursements.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan and United States Launch Enhanced Strategic Partnership Dialogue
incidents.description: Uzbek Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held the first meeting of the Enhanced Strategic Partnership Dialogue in Samarkand. They discussed implementation of previous commitments and cooperation in trade, investment, energy, critical minerals, advanced technologies, education, and security. The event inaugurated a bilateral dialogue mechanism, separate from the C5+1 ministerial session.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan Joins US-Led Artemis Accords on Peaceful Space Exploration
incidents.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov signed the Artemis Accords in Samarkand, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio witnessing the signing. Uzbekistan became the 77th signatory to the nonbinding international principles for peaceful, transparent civil space exploration. The two governments also discussed opportunities for future cooperation in space technology.

incidents.title: Uzbekistan and ReElement Technologies Agree to Develop Critical Minerals Pilot
incidents.description: Uzbek Investment, Industry and Trade Minister Laziz Kudratov met ReElement Technologies director Mark Laverghetta in Samarkand to discuss advanced processing of critical minerals and technology transfer. The two sides agreed to develop and launch a joint pilot project; the ministry did not specify funding, location, or implementation dates.

incidents.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister and Boeing Discuss Possible Aircraft Purchases
incidents.description: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev met Boeing vice president Mike Schnabel in Samarkand to discuss possible aircraft sales to Kyrgyz airlines. Talks also covered commercial proposals, potential financing from the US Export–Import Bank, maintenance services, and aviation infrastructure. No aircraft order or financing agreement was announced.

incidents.title: Kyrgyz and US Foreign Ministers Discuss Investment and Technology
incidents.description: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio during the Samarkand C5+1 ministerial. They discussed political dialogue, trade and investment, and opportunities for US technology in mining, energy, information technology, transport, and finance. The Kyrgyz foreign ministry did not announce any new bilateral agreement.

incidents.title: Rubio and Kazakh Foreign Minister Discuss Energy, Technology, and Natural Resources
incidents.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Kazakhstan Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi in Samarkand to discuss bilateral economic cooperation, including information and communications technology infrastructure, energy security, and natural resources. They also discussed security cooperation and Kazakhstan's commitment to join the Abraham Accords. No new project contract was announced.

incidents.title: Tajik and US Foreign Ministers Discuss Investment and Regional Security
incidents.description: Tajik Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the Samarkand C5+1 meeting. The sides discussed bilateral relations, possible expansion of trade and investment ties, and regional security and stability. No new agreements were reported.

incidents.title: Turkmen and US Foreign Ministers Schedule Future Political Consultations
incidents.description: Turkmen Foreign Minister Rashid Meredov met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Samarkand, joined by Special Envoy Sergio Gor. Both sides reviewed bilateral cooperation and outlined a schedule of upcoming high-level meetings and political consultations. The Turkmen Foreign Ministry did not report any agreement or investment contract.

incidents.title: Uzbek Digital Minister Discusses Government Cloud Technology with Google Cloud
incidents.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Digital Technologies Sherzod Shermatov met Google Cloud government-relations executive Marcin Krasuski during the C5+1 meetings in Samarkand. Discussions covered the use of cloud solutions by public agencies, digital transformation, and the development of national digital infrastructure. The sides agreed to continue discussions; no contract was reported.

incidents.title: Moscow Hosts Eighth Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan
incidents.description: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with representatives from Afghanistan, China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan during the eighth Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan. During his opening speech, Lavrov claimed the Taliban was able to force NATO and U.S. forces to withdraw from Afghanistan after 20 years of occupation through their resilience. Lavrov also emphasized Moscow’s “zero-tolerance” for the deployment of NATO military infrastructure to Afghanistan and its neighboring states and that such a presence could lead to greater instability and conflict.

incidents.title: Data Center Strikes Disrupt Yandex Services in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan
incidents.description: Yandex, Russia’s largest tech company with ride-hailing, delivery, and cloud services widely used in Central Asia, was hit with strikes on three of its data centers between October 8 and 11, disrupting taxi, delivery, and other digital services in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. The first strike on October 8 hit a facility in the Ryazan region housing two AI supercomputers, forcing a complete shut down. This was followed by a strike hitting a data center in Kaluga, disabling some of its equipment. Then, on October 11, another strike hit a data center in Vladimir, Russia, resulting in a complete shutdown. As a result, Yandex users in Kazakhstan experienced disruptions in scooter rentals and ordering taxis, meals, and groceries. Users in Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan reported similar issues.

incidents.title: Russia’s FESCO Expands Rail Services to China, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan
incidents.description: Russian transport group FESCO expanded its Caravan Shuttle rail services to include shipments from Urumqi, China, Kazakhstan via the Khorgos-Altynkol border crossing and through Kazakhstan to Uzbekistan. FESCO plans to operate regular shipments from Urumqi at least monthly, transporting a wide range of cargo, including consumer goods, industrial products, equipment, and components from Chinese makers to customer warehouses in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan.

incidents.title: Belarus Hosts CSTO Joint Military Exercises
incidents.description: Military contingents from Belarus, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan are holding joint military exercises from October 12 to October 16 through the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO). The drills reportedly involve over 1,500 military personnel, over 300 pieces of military equipment, and approximately 80 drones. CSTO said the drills focus on training their “peacekeeping forces” and responding to biological threats which CSTO Deputy Secretary-General Mirlan Turgunbekov said are “particularly relevant given the escalating military and political situation.”

incidents.title: Russia Surpasses China, USA, in Humanitarian Aid to Tajikistan
incidents.description: Humanitarian aid to Tajikistan between January and September dropped 46.3% year-on-year, from $47.17 million to $21.8 million. While Chinese aid fell from $15.9 million to $2.7 million, Russian aid rose from $3.1 million to $7.4 million, and US aid fell from $11.3 million to $5.1 million. Russia jumped from the 3rd largest donor to largest donor amid a sharp pullback in aid from the USA and China.

incidents.title: Russia, Kyrgyzstan Sign Military Cooperation Agreement for 2027
incidents.description: Before the CIS Council of Defense Ministers meeting in Cholpon-Ata, Russian Defense Minister Andrei Belousov and Kyrgyz Defense Minister Ruslan Mukambetov signed a bilateral military cooperation plan for 2027, covering combat training, personnel training, operation of its military base. This comes a day after Belousov visited the Russian naval weapons testing base near Karakol, Kyrgyzstan, one of four Russian military facilities in the country and the State Duma’s ratification of a protocol signed in November 2025 allowing military equipment to be supplied to Kyrgyzstan under contracts between authorized organizations without an import or export license.

incidents.title: Russia, Kazakhstan Launch Pilot Freight Transportation Using e-CMR Technology
incidents.description: Russia and Kazakhstan launched the first pilot international road freight transportation using the e-CMR electronic international consignment note, a project of the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The transport follows the Astana-Moscow route, and its launch marked a practical step toward transport digitalization and cooperation between EAEU states. The use of e-CMR will reduce paperwork costs, accelerate information exchange, and provide real-time access to cargo status.

incidents.title: Russia, Uzbekistan to Hold Cross Days in 2027
